title: Admission funnel: multi-tenant shaping & regional spillover notes
body:
Purpose:
Quick design/experiments checklist for an admission funnel that shapes multi-tenant traffic across regions and degrades gracefully when GPU capacity is constrained. This is an operational-first sketch — lots of open questions below.

High-level goals:
- Keep latency SLOs for high-priority tenants while maximizing throughput and utilization.
- Avoid hard global throttles; prefer soft shaping, spillover, and controlled fallbacks.
- Make control-plane decisions observable and reversible (audit trails + metrics).
- Minimize cross-region cold-starts and avoid cascading failures during global bursts.

Key signals to combine:
- Token accounting per-tenant (logical credits / refill rates)
- Local queue depth (per-ingress node / per-region)
- GPU utilization and occupancy (smoothed 1m/5m windows, percent and tail quantiles)
- Model-specific latency percentiles and current KV cache hit rate
- Recent error rates (OOMs, model failures) and infra degradation signals

Admission funnel stages (conceptual):
1) Ingress pre-check: quick rejects for invalid auth, then soft admit estimation (cheap heuristics).
2) Token handshake: consult per-tenant token ledger to determine immediate allowance.
3) Local queue admission: if local queue >Q_high, attempt immediate spillover to other compatible regions/pools.
4) GPU push: dispatch to serving runtime with a deadline and optional hedging policy.
5) Post-decision feedback: increment/decrement tokens, emit telemetry, update tenant feedback.

Token model (practical variant):
- Each tenant has tokens representing concurrency or tokenized cost units. Tokens refill at tenant-configured rate R (per-second) and burst capacity B.
- For hosted-tier tenants R and B derived from tenant plan; for enterprise reserved capacity tenants, R tied to seat/commit.
- Tokens charged on admit: charge = cost_estimate(request) = base + alpha * estimated_output_tokens + model_weight.
- Use a leaky-bucket enforcement locally to smooth short bursts; global token ledger is eventually consistent.

Refill & reconciliation notes:
- Local ingress nodes keep a cached token balance for low-latency checks. Refill is local per-node using last-known global delta.
- Control plane periodically reconciles balances (every 5–30s) and pushes corrections. Conflicts resolved using timestamped deltas and a bounded drift policy.
- Important: design for stale reads — allow bounded overcommit with overcommit_limit per-node and a hard correction path when reconciliation detects overspend.

Queue-depth and GPU-signal coupling:
- Primary admission decision should be token-first, then queue-depth and GPU signals to gate issuance.
- Define three queue thresholds: Q_warn (start shedding non-critical), Q_soft (deny new low-priority), Q_hard (reject nearly everything).
- GPU occupancy hysteresis: when GPU_util > U_high for >T_high and queue growing, raise per-tenant effective token cost (dynamic surcharge) rather than immediate hard deny. This incentivizes clients to reduce load or accept fallbacks.

Spillover & routing policies:
- Spillover is region-aware and model-compatible aware. Preference order: same-region spare pool -> adjacent-region low-latency pool -> cheapest compatible model in region -> fall back to smaller/quantized model -> deny.
- Maintain regional capacity fingerprints (types, sequence-length-optimized kernels, quantization compatibility) in control plane for routing decisions.
- Respect data residency flags: some tenants opt-out of cross-region spillover. Mark those as non-spillable.

Soft quotas, credit borrowing, and grace periods:
- Provide short grace windows (30–120s) where tenants can borrow a small percentage (e.g., 10–20%) beyond token balance, tracked as debt. Debt repaid by reducing refill rate temporarily.
- Debt should be visible in billing/alerts and bounded by risk tiers. If debt > threshold, escalate to hard deny.

Feedback patterns to clients:
- Prefer early, informative responses over opaque 429s. Options to return: 202+queue-id (inform approximate wait and position), 429 with Retry-After, or 200 with lower-fidelity fallback result.
- For SDK clients, expose a structured error type that includes: reason, suggested fallback (model id or reduce tokens), estimated wait.

Backpressure and hedging details:
- If request is queued beyond wait_threshold, dispatch a hedged request to a secondary pool with a shorter deadline and accept the first successful reply. This buys latency at the cost of extra tokens; only enable for high-priority paths.
- If entering sustained overload, downgrade hedging aggressiveness gradually.

Control plane considerations:
- The control plane maintains tenant quotas, refill rates, region capacity descriptors, and a ledger of recent token deltas. It must be horizontally scalable and partitioned by tenant-id for low contention.
- Ledger ops should be idempotent and append-only per-shard. Use vector-clock-ish metadata for lightweight conflict resolution.
- Provide a read-only fast path for ingress nodes (cached topology + token snapshot) with reconciliation at configurable intervals.

Observability & metrics to emit (instrumentation checklist):
- admit_decision{tenant,region,result} (allowed/queued/spilled/denied)
- token_balance{tenant,host}
- queue_depth{ingress_node,region}
- gpu_util{region,gpu_type,1m,5m}
- kv_cache_hit{model,region}
- spillover_count{from_region,to_region,tenant}
- debt_level{tenant}
- hedged_requests{success_rate,extra_cost_tokens}
- latency_p90/p99 per-tenant per-model

Experiment ideas (small, measurable):
1) Surcharge vs hard deny: run A/B where group A sees dynamic surcharge (increased token cost) when GPU > 80% and group B sees immediate deny. Measure p99 tail, throughput, and customer-visible failures.
2) Local grace windows: enable 60s debt borrowing for low-tier tenants and track debt repayment and billing impact over 2 weeks.
3) Spillover latency budget: measure median added latency for cross-region spillover under controlled load and determine the safe spill fraction before tail latency degrades.

Open questions / risks:
- How much overcommit can we safely tolerate before reconciliation churn causes cascading rejects? Need sims.
- Token accounting consistency: do we prefer stronger consistency for enterprise tenants with reserved capacity? (Probably yes — separate ledger mode).
- Client SDK adoption: will clients implement suggested fallbacks or will they retry aggressively? Need SDK heuristics + server-side retry budget.
- Cost accounting: hedging and spillover increase token burn — how to make this visible in per-tenant billing and SLA reports?

Action items / next steps:
- Build a small simulator that models: tokens, local cache drift, reconciliation interval, queue thresholds, and GPU utilization patterns. Run stress scenarios (diurnal spike + sudden global burst). Owner: Miguel.
- Prototype local ingress behavior: cached token snapshot + overcommit window with reconciliation correction. Owner: Evelyn.
- Draft a telemetry dashboard with the metrics above and add alerts for queue depth > Q_soft for >2m in any region. Owner: Ravi.

Notes-to-self / rough heuristics we liked:
- Default overcommit per-ingress-node: 5% of tenant burst cap or max 10 tokens (whichever smaller).
- Q_warn = 0.6 * queue_capacity; Q_soft = 0.85; Q_hard = 0.98.
- GPU Util hysteresis windows: 1m for detect, 5m for sustained.

References & links (internal):
- Confluence: Capacity playbook (linked_artifacts)
- Git: ingress-governor PR for local-cache token handling
- Slack: #platform-admission thread id 2392

Unresolved: add sample pseudocode for token refill+admit? Quick sketch below.

Pseudocode (admit path)
---
function admit_request(req):
  tenant = req.tenant_id
  cost = estimate_cost(req)
  balance = local_cache.get_balance(tenant)
  if balance + overcommit_allowed >= cost:
    if queue_depth(node) > Q_hard:
      record_decision(tenant, \"denied_queue_full\")
      return Deny(\"queue_full\")
    if gpu_util_high(region) and low_priority(req):
      record_decision(tenant, \"surcharge\")
      cost = cost * surcharge_factor
    local_cache.subtract(tenant, cost)
    enqueue_to_runtime(req)
    record_decision(tenant, \"admitted\")
    return Accept(queue_id)
  else:
    if can_spillover(req):
      attempt_spill(req)
      record_decision(tenant, \"spilled\")
      return SpillResponse
    else:
      return Deny(\"insufficient_tokens\")
---

Comment: keep this doc small and iterative — plan to convert to a more formal playbook once sims give numbers.
summary: Draft notes for a multi-tenant admission funnel that merges token accounting, queue depth, and GPU signals. Includes stages, heuristics, metrics, experiments, open questions and action items.
